visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: In a sale process, what is a first-round bid?

options.text: A binding offer the seller can accept
A non-binding range to reach round two
A final price set after due diligence
A public offer made to all shareholders

questions.explain: First-round bids are indicative and based only on the information memorandum. The highest one doesn't win; it buys a place in the second round.
questions.explain_at: A first-round bid is a ticket to the next round

questions.q: Bidder A offers 1,050 with a one in ten chance its financing fails. Bidder B offers 1,000, fully financed. Which is worth more to the seller?

options.text: A, since 1,050 beats 1,000
Equal, since both are about 1,000
A, worth about 995 after the risk
B, since A is worth about 945

questions.explain: 90% × 1,050 ≈ 945, already below B's 1,000, and a failed sale leaves the seller worse off than where it started.
questions.explain_at: Ninety percent of one thousand and fifty is about nine hundred and forty-five

questions.q: What's the difference between signing and closing?

options.text: Signing is the promise; closing is when money changes hands
Signing is non-binding; closing makes the deal binding
Signing is when the buyer pays; closing is the board vote
Signing is the announcement; closing ends due diligence

questions.explain: Signing commits both sides; closing comes once the conditions, such as regulatory approvals and any shareholder vote, are met. Twitter signed in April and closed in October.
questions.explain_at: Third trap. Signing is the binding promise

questions.q: Which part of the merger agreement let Twitter force Elon Musk to complete the deal?

options.text: The reverse termination fee
The material adverse change clause
Specific performance
The poison pill

questions.explain: Specific performance lets a court order the buyer to complete rather than just pay damages. The $1bn fee applied only in set cases, so it didn't buy Musk a way out.
questions.explain_at: The contract gave Twitter the right to specific performance

questions.q: Octus is priced at about $3.5bn, with EBITDA of about $145m this year. Roughly what multiple of this year's EBITDA is that?

options.text: About 17.5x
About 24x
About 2.7x
About 35x

questions.explain: $3.5bn ÷ $145m ≈ 24x. Dividing by next year's $200m gives 17.5x, the number Sofia picked; say which year you're using.
questions.explain_at: On this year's one hundred and forty-five million, it's about twenty-four times
